Real-time Write and Read#

Real-time mode makes writes visible to queries in the same process before a snapshot commit. A shared RealtimeContext owns the uncommitted stores; queries combine an immutable view of those stores with committed table files. Readers without that context see only committed files.

Real-time storage is pluggable through the RealtimeStore interface. The default implementation uses Apache Arrow to buffer rows and serve reads. Applications can provide their own RealtimeStoreFactory through RealtimeContext::Create(factory) to customize storage and retrieval while keeping Paimon’s real-time write, read, and commit lifecycle.

Durability still comes from snapshot commits. Upstream must retain replayable input and provide monotonically increasing offsets for each partition-bucket. Real-time operations currently support only the main branch. Use a separate context for each table, and coordinate a single active writer for each partition-bucket.

Modes and Capabilities#

The table schema and options select the mode; there is no separate realtime.mode option.

Mode

Selection

Uncommitted state

Query semantics

Append

No primary key; no real-time deduplicate key

Arrow batches in write order

Concatenate committed files and the visible memory tail

PK MOR

Primary key; deletion-vectors.enabled=false

Batches sorted by primary key and sequence number

Merge disk runs, sealed batches, and building batches by primary key

PK DV

Primary key; deletion-vectors.enabled=true

The same sorted PK store as PK MOR

Apply committed DVs, then merge disk and memory by primary key

Append deduplicate

Append table with realtime.deduplicate-key-fields set and deletion-vectors.enabled=true

Mark superseded rows in an in-memory DV during writes; persist DV files at commit

Full predicate pushdown; apply the in-memory DV to disk and memory reads without MOR

All four modes support read-before-prepare, sealed-but-uncommitted reads, partition-bucket isolation, offset-aware commit and recovery, immutable read views, projection, and optional sealed-segment spill with the default store. The shared read pipeline also handles nested projection, selected MAP keys, and supported VARIANT access over physical store fields. Predicate pruning and exact residual filtering follow the mode-specific rules below.

Append accepts INSERT only. PK and append deduplicate also accept UPDATE_AFTER, DELETE, and UPDATE_BEFORE. PK supports composite primary keys, but its real-time merge engine is currently limited to merge-engine=deduplicate. Append deduplicate currently accepts exactly one non-null, non-nested key field and is experimental: its persisted index format may change.

PK DV and append deduplicate are different designs. PK DV retains primary-key merge semantics; append deduplicate uses a persisted stable row offset and does not turn the table into a primary-key table.

Configuration#

Common Options#

Option

Default

Meaning

realtime.enabled

false

Enables real-time operations. The builders must also receive a shared RealtimeContext to select process-local writing and union reading.

realtime.spill-enabled

false

The default store synchronously spills frozen Arrow data to temporary IPC files during explicit Seal. Prepare does not trigger spill.

realtime.read-view-ttl

5 min

Positive lifetime of a scan’s read-view ticket before reader creation.

realtime.store.stats-mode

none

none or full. Full mode collects per-batch min/max and null counts for conservative predicate pruning, including retained spill metadata.

realtime.deduplicate-key-fields

Unset

Selects append deduplicate mode. Although expressed as a comma-separated list, currently exactly one field is accepted.

bucket

Must be set

Real-time mode requires fixed buckets: bucket > 0.

read.batch-size

1024

Maximum raw batch size returned by the default store’s query readers; not the number of visible rows after bitmap filtering.

spill-compression

zstd

Compression used by temporary spill files.

spill-compression.zstd-level

1

Compression level when using Zstandard.

Set WriteContextBuilder::WithTempDirectory() when enabling spill. The default factory rejects spill without a non-empty temporary directory or a file system. Spill is explicit at seal boundaries; the normal write-buffer memory manager does not automatically bound real-time store memory.

Setting realtime.enabled=true alone does not attach an in-process store. This permits a separate ordinary writer to compact committed files without joining the real-time context. It does not permit ordinary row writes into an append deduplicate table.

Mode-specific Setup#

For append mode, create a table without primary keys and use:

bucket = 4
realtime.enabled = true

For PK MOR, define the table’s primary keys and use:

bucket = 4
realtime.enabled = true
merge-engine = deduplicate
deletion-vectors.enabled = false

For PK DV, define primary keys and enable DVs instead:

bucket = 4
realtime.enabled = true
merge-engine = deduplicate
deletion-vectors.enabled = true

Both PK modes use the same real-time writer and store. PK DV uses the normal PK deletion-vector and compaction infrastructure; it does not require the append deduplicate .offset sidecar or an offset bitmap file index.

For append deduplicate, create a table with no primary keys. Its schema must contain _REALTIME_OFFSET BIGINT NOT NULL and a non-null key, for example id BIGINT NOT NULL. Deduplication is scoped to a partition: the same key may exist independently in different partitions. The bucket key must use only deduplicate key fields; applications are responsible for assigning rows to the correct bucket. For example, use bucket-key=id:

bucket = 4
bucket-key = id
realtime.enabled = true
realtime.deduplicate-key-fields = id
deletion-vectors.enabled = true
deletion-vectors.bitmap64 = false
file-index.read.enabled = true
file-index.bitmap.columns = _REALTIME_OFFSET

The two indexes serve different purposes:

  • The .offset sidecar looks up existing offsets by deduplicate key during writes, so superseded rows can be marked in the in-memory DV.

  • file-index.bitmap.columns=_REALTIME_OFFSET builds an offset index used during queries to quickly map in-memory DV offsets to exact file row positions and filter those rows.

The offset column must have an index supporting exact BIGINT IN and NOT_IN row-position matching. Among Paimon’s default plugins, supported choices include bitmap, bsi, and range-bitmap. Indexes may be embedded in file metadata or stored in an external file-index file. Approximate indexes such as Bloom filters are insufficient.

Index capabilities are checked when creating a table and loading its schema, not for each file during reads. Applications must keep the index configuration consistent with existing files and ensure that those files have compatible exact indexes.

The bitmap64 prohibition concerns persisted file DVs; logical deleted offsets are still represented by RoaringBitmap64 in memory.

The .offset sidecar lookup uses cache-page-size, lookup.cache-max-memory-size, and lookup.cache.high-priority-pool-ratio. These configure its lookup cache, not a total memory limit for the real-time store.

Input Schema and Offsets#

Offsets are application-assigned, non-negative int64 values scoped to one logical partition-bucket. They must be strictly increasing within each input batch and across subsequent batches. Gaps are allowed; reuse or backward movement is rejected. INT64_MAX cannot be an input offset because the exclusive end must also fit in int64.

Mode

FileStoreWrite::Write input layout

Persisted offset

Append

[_REALTIME_OFFSET, table fields...]

Internal prefix removed before writing data files

PK MOR / PK DV

[_REALTIME_OFFSET, table fields...]

Internal prefix removed before writing data files

Append deduplicate

Table schema in its declared field order, including _REALTIME_OFFSET

Normal table column retained in data files and compaction output

Do not add the internal offset prefix to the formal table schema in ordinary append or PK mode. In append deduplicate mode, do not add a second prefix: the offset is already a formal field and may occupy any declared position.

Construct Arrow batches in the required layout and set their partition and bucket with RecordBatchBuilder::SetPartition() and SetBucket(). Routing and offset assignment belong to the application. Deduplication never crosses partition-bucket boundaries.

For PK writes, the framework adds _SEQUENCE_NUMBER and _VALUE_KIND and sorts each stored batch by primary key, then sequence number. Input offsets are validated before sorting. The sequence number, not the numeric offset, resolves PK versions; application-defined sequence.field is not supported by real-time PK mode.

An OffsetRange is half-open: [begin, end). It is an event-progress envelope, not a row count. For example, input offsets 10, 12, 15 cover [10, 16). Deletes consume offsets even when they produce no data-file row, so a delete-only prepare can advance progress with an empty data increment.

API Lifecycle#

Use the same RealtimeContext for writing, planning, and reading. Enable streaming mode on the writer for progress-aware checkpoints; real-time union queries themselves use batch scans.

The snippets below run inside a Status or Result-returning function using the paimon namespace. They assume an existing native table, table_path, a stable commit_user, the mode-specific options map, and an input batch built as described above.

PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::shared_ptr<RealtimeContext> realtime,
                       RealtimeContext::Create());

WriteContextBuilder write_builder(table_path, commit_user);
write_builder.SetOptions(options)
    .WithStreamingMode(true)
    .WithRealtimeContext(realtime);
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::unique_ptr<WriteContext> write_context,
                       write_builder.Finish());
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::unique_ptr<FileStoreWrite> writer,
                       FileStoreWrite::Create(std::move(write_context)));
PAIMON_RETURN_NOT_OK(writer->Write(std::move(batch)));

To query before preparing or committing:

ScanContextBuilder scan_builder(table_path);
scan_builder.SetOptions(options).WithRealtimeContext(realtime);
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::unique_ptr<ScanContext> scan_context,
                       scan_builder.Finish());
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::unique_ptr<TableScan> scan,
                       TableScan::Create(std::move(scan_context)));
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::shared_ptr<Plan> plan, scan->CreatePlan());

ReadContextBuilder read_builder(table_path);
read_builder.SetOptions(options).WithRealtimeContext(realtime);
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::unique_ptr<ReadContext> read_context,
                       read_builder.Finish());
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::unique_ptr<TableRead> read,
                       TableRead::Create(std::move(read_context)));
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::unique_ptr<BatchReader> reader,
                       read->CreateReader(plan->Splits()));
// Consume NextBatch() or NextBatchWithBitmap(), then Close() the reader.

Apply the same query predicate to scan and read. If exact residual filtering must happen inside the library, call ReadContextBuilder::EnablePredicateFilter(true). File and batch statistics are conservative pruning, not a substitute for evaluating the user predicate.

Checkpoint with progress-aware APIs:

const int64_t checkpoint_id = 1;
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::vector<RealtimeCommitProgress> progress,
                       writer->PrepareCommitWithProgress(checkpoint_id));

CommitContextBuilder commit_builder(table_path, commit_user);
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::unique_ptr<CommitContext> commit_context,
                       commit_builder.SetOptions(options).Finish());
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(std::unique_ptr<FileStoreCommit> commit,
                       FileStoreCommit::Create(std::move(commit_context)));
PAIMON_ASSIGN_OR_RAISE(
    int64_t snapshot_id,
    commit->CommitWithProgress(progress, checkpoint_id, /*watermark=*/std::nullopt));
PAIMON_RETURN_NOT_OK(writer->RefreshCommittedSnapshot(snapshot_id));
PAIMON_RETURN_NOT_OK(writer->Close());

The operations have different responsibilities:

  1. Write publishes rows to the process-local building store.

  2. Optional Seal freezes a segment, opens a new building segment, and may spill. It does not create a committed snapshot or prepare data-file messages.

  3. PrepareCommitWithProgress freezes the current building segment without spilling and writes it together with earlier sealed segments to table data files, returning their offset ranges together with commit messages. It does not publish a snapshot or reclaim the real-time data.

  4. CommitWithProgress atomically publishes files, indexes, and the updated partition-bucket offset map. The snapshot’s realtime.offsets property references a metadata file containing the durable progress.

  5. RefreshCommittedSnapshot loads the committed progress and reclaims fully covered sealed segments. Deduplicate refresh also replaces the active file-key lookup atomically with memory/DV advancement.

Keep every prepared-but-uncommitted RealtimeCommitProgress entry. If a later checkpoint subsumes earlier prepares, pass the complete outstanding prefix to commit, not just the latest prepare result. Offset gaps make omitted prepares indistinguishable from valid sparse input, and skipping one can cause data loss.

CommitMessage serialization does not contain the progress range or the deduplicate deleted_offsets bitmap. Preserve the complete progress when coordinating checkpoints. Snapshot conflicts are retried internally against the latest snapshot; commit identifiers must follow the streaming commit protocol. With a version-managed catalog, configure the writer and committer with the same WithCatalog() catalog and identifier.

Read Views and Consistency#

Planning first pins immutable memory views and then plans committed disk data. For each active partition-bucket it captures two exclusive bounds:

disk:   progress covered by the selected snapshot
memory: [committed_end_offset, memory_end_offset)

Filtering memory by these bounds prevents duplicate reads after a commit and excludes writes after the captured memory view. Existing views remain valid across later writes, seals, spill publication, and refresh-driven reclamation.

Ordinary append scans keep earlier disk splits independently schedulable and attach the memory view to a tail split. PK and append deduplicate group a partition-bucket’s disk splits with its memory view so that merge or pending deletion semantics cover the whole bucket.

A real-time split carries an opaque read-view ticket. Resolve it with the same context in the same process. Successful reader creation consumes the ticket; failed creation retains it until its TTL expires. Once a reader is created, the reader pins its view independently of ticket expiry. Replan if a ticket expires, or if a previously consumed split needs to be read again.

An explicit snapshot id is accepted only if its progress is not behind the context’s reclaimed progress for relevant active stores. It does not restore an old in-memory state and is not unrestricted historical time travel. For a disk-only historical query, do not attach the real-time context.

Implementation by Mode#

Append#

RealtimeAppendOnlyWriter validates offsets and writes to an APPEND_ONLY store. The default ArrowRealtimeStore retains building batches and immutable sealed segments in write order. Query readers project the requested fields, optionally prune stored batches using statistics, and apply the visible offset range before removing the hidden offset column.

Preparing reads sealed segments through the ordinary AppendOnlyWriter, removing the internal offset prefix before writing table files. Queries do not need key lookup or version merge; disk and memory readers are concatenated.

Primary Key MOR#

RealtimePrimaryKeyWriter materializes PK transport batches with sequence number, row kind, and offset. Each sorted batch is an independent merge input; multiple stored batches do not form a single globally sorted stream.

Query construction merges sorted disk sections and the memory readers, applies deduplicate merge semantics, and drops final delete records. It collects all disk splits belonging to the active partition-bucket, rather than merging memory against only one disk split. Preparing similarly merges the sealed streams before handing them to MergeTreeWriter to write normal PK files.

Only primary-key predicates are safe to push into unresolved versions. A predicate on a value column must be evaluated after version merge: filtering out the newest value first could incorrectly expose an older matching value.

Primary Key DV#

PK DV uses the same real-time PK write and sequence-number logic. During a union read, committed file DVs remove already-invalid physical rows, but L0 runs and memory may still contain duplicate keys and delete records. The final reader therefore still performs a primary-key merge across disk and memory.

For real-time scans, L0 is retained instead of being skipped as in the normal DV batch scan. Predicate handling distinguishes storage levels:

  • High-level files (level > 0) can use the full predicate for statistics and file-index pruning under committed DV semantics.

  • L0 and memory receive only primary-key predicates before merge.

  • The full residual predicate is applied after merge when explicitly enabled in the read context.

Enabling DVs does not make uncommitted PK data append-only and does not make arbitrary value-predicate pushdown safe for L0 or memory.

Append Deduplicate / Offset DV#

This mode uses two independent lookup directions:

key -> logical offset(s)                  memory key indexes / .offset sidecars
logical offset -> physical row positions  exact _REALTIME_OFFSET file index

For each write, RealtimeDeduplicateWriter looks up existing keys across committed files, sealed segments, and the building segment. Matching old offsets are marked deleted, and within-batch duplicates are resolved in row order. Add rows are appended to the store; delete events update only the key/DV state, without persisting a delete row.

Key indexes and DV bitmaps use copy-on-write snapshots, so later writes do not change the state held by existing lookups, read views, or seal checkpoints.

Memory reads use the read view’s DV to exclude rows whose offsets are marked deleted.

Disk reads apply both committed file DVs and pending offset deletions. Pending deletions become per-file _REALTIME_OFFSET NOT IN (...) predicates, trimmed using reliable min/max statistics or left untrimmed when statistics are missing or ambiguous. The exact file index enforces these predicates independently of optional residual filtering. The offset is omitted from the final result unless the user selected it.

Prepare retains each seal’s logical deletion checkpoint and writes surviving add rows with their original offsets. Each output file gets a .offset sidecar mapping key fingerprints to offsets, separate from the exact offset file index.

Each commit attempt resolves deleted offsets to row positions in the latest snapshot’s files and the prepared new files, then merges them into the committed file DVs. Repeating this resolution on retries handles file changes caused by conflicting commits or compaction.

Spill and Memory Accounting#

The default store freezes the current building data and opens a new building segment under a short lock. Explicit Seal writes the frozen segment to an Arrow IPC spill file outside the write lock when spill is enabled. Prepare freezes without spilling and writes directly to table data files, reading any earlier spilled segments as needed. There is no background spill worker: the seal/prepare thread waits for its I/O, while another thread can write to the new building segment.

Deduplicate uses two-phase seal to freeze data, key index, offset range, and DV checkpoint at the same boundary. The frozen segment remains queryable and its keys remain discoverable while spill is in progress. Only after writing and closing the file successfully is its stored representation replaced. A spill failure keeps the in-memory segment and cleans up the incomplete file, but is still terminal for the owning writer/context.

Old views can retain the memory representation after spill or reclamation; new views use the published representation. Spill files are deleted when the store and all remaining handles/readers have released them. They are temporary storage, not a recoverable log after process restart. Deduplicate key indexes and DVs remain in memory; full-mode statistics also remain resident after spill.

RealtimeContext::GetMetrics() and real-time writer metrics expose:

  • realtimeBuildingMemoryBytes, realtimeSealedMemoryBytes, realtimeTotalMemoryBytes;

  • realtimeBuildingRowCount, realtimeSealedRowCount, realtimeTotalRowCount.

These are current store accounting, not process RSS or a visible-row count. Rows include stored versions hidden by merge/DV filtering. Memory counts include Arrow buffers and retained statistics; deduplicate also counts retained key-map buffers, row-offset bitmaps, and distinct deletion checkpoints.

Recovery, Schema Changes, and Compaction#

Recovery and Failure Handling#

Read durable progress with RealtimeSnapshotOffsets::ReadAllOffsets() or ReadOffset() from a committed snapshot. Replay starting at the returned offset. If ReadOffset() returns -1 for a partition-bucket, use the upstream’s initial position.

A new context restores committed progress, but uncommitted data requires upstream replay. Reusing a healthy context preserves its uncommitted tail; retain any outstanding prepared progress when replacing the writer.

After a write/flush, seal, prepare, or terminal progress-commit failure, discard the writer and context and recover from the latest committed progress. Closing with unprepared data also invalidates the context. Prepare alone is not durable: retain prepared progress until commit, even after the writer closes.

Schema Changes#

Reusing a live store requires the same physical schema and mode. After a schema change, recreate the context and writer and replay uncommitted input. data-evolution.enabled is not supported in real-time mode.

Deduplicate reads and lookups support historical file schemas, which must remain available together with their key options. Key renames and field reordering are supported when key field ID, type, and non-nullability stay compatible. _REALTIME_OFFSET must retain its name, field ID, and non-null int64 type.

Compaction and Destructive Operations#

The real-time writer does not compact files automatically or support explicit Compact. Use a separate ordinary compaction writer without WithRealtimeContext(), then refresh to the resulting snapshot.

Append deduplicate compaction preserves surviving offsets, rebuilds indexes, and remaps the latest deletions to the output files. External rewrites must not drop the required offsets or indexes.

Overwrite, truncate, partition drop, and rollback may reset progress and are not automatically coordinated with active real-time writers. Stop affected writers, recreate their contexts, and reset the upstream recovery position before resuming.

Extension Points and Current Limits#

RealtimeContext::Create(factory) accepts a custom RealtimeStoreFactory. Custom stores manage buffering, read views, and spill while following the RealtimeStore contracts. Paimon manages table files, indexes, merge semantics, and commits. Append deduplicate also keeps key indexes and DVs in the framework; custom delegates need RealtimeStoreTwoPhaseSeal to enable its spill.

Current restrictions include:

  • Native tables on the main branch with fixed positive bucket counts and full write schemas only.

  • Process-local batch union scans only. Streaming scans, limit pushdown, global-index result splits, vector/full-text search, and count-only real-time readers are unsupported.

  • PK mode supports the deduplicate merge engine with default delete handling, ascending sequence order, and changelog-producer=none. Custom sequence.field, floating-point keys, PK global indexes, lookup without DVs, and read-optimized union scans are unsupported.

  • Append deduplicate requires a single non-null scalar key, a persisted offset column, exact offset file-index reads, and non-bitmap64 DVs. Existing ordinary append files are not migrated automatically.

  • Spill covers Arrow data, not key indexes or DVs, and provides neither a hard memory limit nor crash recovery.

Code Map#

  • include/paimon/realtime/: public context, store, progress, and recovery APIs.

  • src/paimon/core/realtime/: mode-specific writers, default Arrow store, deduplicate wrapper/indexes, schema layout, and memory-read pipeline.

  • src/paimon/core/table/source/realtime_table_scan.cpp: memory pinning, snapshot-progress validation, and partition-bucket split grouping.

  • src/paimon/core/table/source/append_only_table_read.cpp: append union reads and per-file pending offset-DV predicates.

  • src/paimon/core/operation/merge_file_split_read.cpp: PK disk/memory merge and level-aware predicate pushdown.

  • src/paimon/core/operation/commit/realtime_*: durable progress, logical-DV materialization, commit retry, and compaction DV remapping.

  • test/inte/realtime_write_inte_test.cpp: lifecycle and mode-specific integration coverage; store/reader unit tests live next to their implementation.
